title: A workout in progress can be lost if the phone cannot read it back when the app opens
what: When the app opens it reads back the workout that was still going. If that read fails for any reason, the app quietly treats it as no workout, keeps no note of why, and shows nothing. If the member then starts a new workout, the saved one is written over and is gone.
expected: A failed read should be tried again, or the member told the workout could not be reopened, and the saved copy kept until it is read; a note of why should be kept and sent to MettleUp.
fix_line: Retry the read and keep the saved workout untouched until it is read, telling the member if it still fails

title: When records cannot be worked out again after an edit or a past workout, no note is kept of why
what: After editing a workout or logging a past one, the app works the member's records out again. If that fails, the screen says the records may be out of date, but nothing records why. The same is true when the suggested weights quietly fail to load: they just vanish.
expected: Every one of these failures should keep a short note of the reason, so a pattern can be found and fixed.
fix_line: Keep a note of the error in each of these places

title: A moved imported workout can come back twice if one quiet read fails during a re-import
what: A Hevy or Strong re-import knows a workout whose date was changed by its first start time, kept in a small saved list. If reading that list fails, the import carries on as if it were empty, so a moved workout is brought in again as a second copy, with no word and no note.
expected: If the list cannot be read, the import should stop and say so, or skip workouts it cannot tell apart, rather than add copies.
fix_line: Stop the import with a plain message when the saved list cannot be read

items.reason: these folders only read and write the phone's own database; no outside service is called here
no scheduled jobs live in the phone's workout data folders
